body:
[aida:product] AUTONOMY IS RUNNING AGAIN. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED - #2060, please prioritise it, it unblocks every drain.

THE CAUSE, and it is BUG-748 in a second place. A pipelined batch child is spawned as its own `queue work <spec> --auto-complete=through-ci`, so it takes the drain lock at its top while the PARENT batch drive still holds it. The spawn set AIDA_PIPELINED_BATCH_CHILD and AIDA_PIPELINED_RESULT_PATH but NOT AIDA_DRAIN_BORROW. BUG-748 taught the INTEGRATOR child to borrow; the pipelined child never got the same treatment.

IT WAS UNREACHABLE UNTIL pipeline_depth WENT 1 -> 2 ON 2026-09-20. At depth 1 no child ever overlaps a live parent lock. That is why the drain dies from 02:24 on 09-21 and not before - the dates line up exactly with that config change. Whoever raised the depth did nothing wrong; it exposed a latent defect.

VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DRAIN, not just unit tests. Before: every launch died in 5-9 seconds with 1 collision and 0 iterations. After: 0 collisions, drain status active, and it is into a headless implementer phase on BUG-1462 as I write this. 5281 lib tests pass; the unit test is mutation-checked.

I CORRECTED MY OWN FILING AND WANT THAT ON THE RECORD. BUG-1568's description says the drain "collides with itself". That is WRONG, and it is what I acted on first: I implemented the self-collision fix, built it, ran a real drain, AND THE COLLISION SURVIVED. That falsified the reading outright. A child inherits the parent's redirected stdout, so its refusal lands in the same log and names the PARENT as holder - self-collision and child-not-borrowing produce a byte-identical log, and I assumed the simpler one. I reverted that fix; it also contradicted three existing tests that deliberately use the same-process pid as a stand-in for a live holder.

TWO OTHER FALSE LEADS, both caught by checking rather than by being careful:
- "The queue is empty" - I ran `aida queue list` as my own shell user while the drain uses --user role:implementer. That queue has 86 entries. BUG-89's rule, which I had a memory for and still walked into.
- "19 orphaned test files never declared" - I grepped only lib.rs. They are declared in their own subject modules (worktree_scope_gate.rs declares tests/worktree_scope_gate_tests.rs, and so on). Entirely false; not filed. One of the 19 was a file I had created myself moments earlier by appending to a path that did not exist.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX, and it stays open on BUG-1568: the misattribution. A lock refusal is still reported as "drain stopped at BUG-1462 (phase 2 failed)", which routes every reader to an innocent spec. That is what hid this for a day. #2060 removes the condition that produced the message but not the message's capacity to mislead, and the next unrelated failure of the same shape will do it again. I kept them separate on purpose rather than widening the PR.

STILL YOURS AND UNCHANGED: 28 of 30 open approved specs have execution_mode UNSET, so the drain-eligible pool is two specs deep even now that drains work. Grooming a mode is the advisor write. That is now the binding constraint on throughput, not the lock.

ALSO: the launcher (v8) is still stopped - I killed it while diagnosing. Once #2060 merges and the release binary is rebuilt, it should be restarted, or drains only run when someone launches one by hand. I have not restarted it because it would run the OLD binary, which still has the bug.

BOARD: #2060 (this), #2058 merged, #2019 awaiting your F3 call, #1999/#1989 fanned, #1978 frozen.
subject: AUTONOMY RESTORED — #2060 fixes the drain (BUG-748 in a second place, exposed by pipeline_depth 1->2); my own first diagnosis was wrong and I say how
